title: Artin's primitive root conjecture
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: The proof, after OpenAI's 2026 paper, that every integer a other than -1 that is not a square is a primitive root modulo at least c_a x/(log x)^2 primes in (x, 2x). The index of a prime and Kummer fields reduce the theorem to two propositions. A zero-free strip Re s > 1 - 10^-6, uniform over all cyclotomic fields containing the twelfth roots of unity and all their finite-order Hecke characters, comes from a family of cubic Gauss sums: S-integers and sextic reciprocity, Kummer and correction characters, the cubic theta function of Kazhdan and Patterson, norm sheets and exact Gaussian smoothing, a Weyl reflection, a quadratic large sieve, a Poisson probe and its Euler product, and zero detection. The strip gives uniform complete splitting in the Kummer fields Q(mu_q, a^(1/q)). Primes p = crQ + 1 in a progression of quadratic nonresidues come from a block sieve, Bombieri-Vinogradov, marked Type II estimates and Buchstab's densities.
prerequisites: Mertens' estimates, the Gamma function, entire functions of order one, convexity in the critical strip, the prime number theorem, Hadamard's three circles theorem (course The Riemann zeta function, NT-ZETA-02, NT-ZETA-03, NT-ZETA-05, NT-ZETA-06, NT-ZETA-09, NT-ZETA-18)
the Siegel-Walfisz and Bombieri-Vinogradov theorems (course Dirichlet L-functions and primes in progressions, NT-DIRL-11, NT-DIRL-15)
explicit formulas for L-functions (course Explicit formulas and positivity, NT-EXPF-02)
adeles, ideles, Poisson summation on the adeles, Hecke characters, Tate's thesis and Hecke L-functions (course Adeles, ideles and Tate's thesis, NT-ADL-02 to NT-ADL-10)
units, discriminants and the different, ramification, cyclotomic fields, counting ideals of bounded norm (course Number fields)
Kummer theory, Hilbert symbols, power residue symbols and reciprocity laws, the global reciprocity law, ring class fields, Artin L-functions (course Class field theory)
Hensel's lemma, places in extensions and the product formula, the multiplicative group of a local field (course Local fields, NT-LOC-03, NT-LOC-05, NT-LOC-11)

discharged_obligations.statement: N5 one-sided marked Type II estimate: for fixed delta, C, D_* > 0 and q in (0, 1), with H_m, H_n >= x^delta and X = H_m H_n of order x, a group-invariant F with |F| <= 1, alpha_m = m^(iv) (1_{m prime} - 1_{P^-(m) > W}/(V(W) log m)) on an interval in [H_m, 2H_m] with |v| <= L^C, and beta_n supported on W-rough integers in [H_n, 2H_n] with |beta_n| <= L^C, the sum of alpha_m beta_n F(mn - 1) W(mn - 1) is at most C' X L^(-D_*) once the number K of prime groups is large in terms of delta, C, D_*, q, independently of the group exponents (OpenAI, The Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors, OpenAI Math Release preprint, 24 Sep 2026, Theorem 3.1, https://github.com/openai/math/tree/main/preprints/The-Poisson-Dirichlet-Law-for-Prime-Predecessors-September-24-2026). Stated in lesson 17, Section 2. Intended home: a course on the Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors.
discharged_obligations.comparison: Theorem 2.3 states N5 for the same coefficient m^(iv)(1_prime - 1_(P^-(m) > W)/(V(W) log m)) on an interval I in [H_m, 2H_m] with |v| <= L^C, the same marks, group-invariant F and W-rough beta, under x/c_* <= X <= c_* x, uniformly in I and v. It is at least as strong: the threshold K_0 depends only on C and D_* (N5 allows dependence on delta and q as well). Its proof is Theorem 2.2 together with Corollary 2.2 of long-prime-polynomials.

discharged_obligations.statement: N6 coefficient criterion: N5 holds with alpha replaced by any sequence supported on W-rough integers of an interval in [H_m, 2H_m] with |alpha_m| <= L^C, provided that for all fixed A_0, B, A > 0, every Dirichlet character chi of modulus at most L^(A_0) and every |t| <= 2 X L^B, |(1/H_m) sum alpha_m chi(m) m^(it)| <= C_A L^(-A) uniformly (OpenAI-029, Lemma 10.2, extracted from the proof of N5 in Sections 3-5 of the Poisson-Dirichlet preprint). Stated in lesson 17, Section 2; used for Proposition 5.1 of lesson 17 and Lemma 2.1 of lesson 18. Intended home: the same course as N5.
discharged_obligations.comparison: Theorem 2.2 assumes alpha supported on W-rough integers of [H_m, 2H_m] (not necessarily an interval), |alpha_m| <= L^C, and twisted cancellation (Definition 2.1, the same condition as (2.2) of N6 with constants C_tc(A_0, B, A)); beta, F and the marks as in N5. K_0 depends only on C and D_*; the bound is uniform in F, the supports and the coefficients. At least as strong as N6. Proof in lessons 7 to 17 of the course, completed in Section 4 of the-major-term-and-the-theorem.

Stated in lesson 17, Section 2; used for Lemma 4.1 and Proposition 5.1 of lesson 17. Intended home: a lesson on Vinogradov's mean value method and the zero-free region at large height in the course on the Riemann zeta function (NT-ZETA).
discharged_obligations.comparison: N7(1): Theorem 1.1 of long-prime-polynomials holds for x^tau/2 <= N <= x^(1/tau), moduli q <= L^(C_0), L^(A+8) <= |t| <= x^2 and every interval in [N, 2N], with a constant depending on tau, C_0, A; since theta < 1 <= 1/tau it contains N7(1), with B_0 = A + 8. N7(2): Theorem 2.1 of a-mean-value-theorem-and-logarithmic-phases-at-large-height (T = log L) has the same ranges with constant 1 and C_3 = 10.
